title: Signs in Egypt and the Nature of the Heavens
english: Therefore, the mountains of the earth, flowing with milk and honey, are called mountains of beasts and of food, from which he says that God will be seen manifest and exceedingly great. And then the proud shall suffer the things laid before them, not even finding their hands to do anything, as if being carried away by a stupor. For you startled them, your people and those appointed to you, defending territories, as if to join the False horse to salvation, and 'These in chariots and horses, but we in the name of the Lord our God will call upon' (Ps 20:8); they themselves stumbled and fell, but we arose and were upright. The same thing is revealed here through the stumbling and the fall, by means of the being carried away and the hardening.

The Confessor thus interpreted: 'For the fury of man shall confess to you, a remnant of fury being girded around' (Ps 75:11). Since the hot-tempered one, acting in anger and towards wrath in all things, not towards righteousness, is subject to confessions and to recognitions concerning those things of which he sins. For fury is easy toward sin, even daring unto murder, so that the reasoning remaining with him in the soul brings forth strong thoughts of repentance, surrounding the whole soul regarding the things done and said not rightly through fury.

From what is laid before us until the second verse, the word will proceed through the difficult and the painful things concerning the people, and thus leads into brighter things following (Ps 76 argument). He says in the present psalm that there is much time in which the nation may sufficiently encompass and the hope of help from God, unless someone, remembering the former things, might be strengthened into the hope of the coming good things.

Thus, even if he has blessed piously in the first verse, he thus introduces weak reasonings that weigh down men in the longer evils (Ps 76:2,3). For now, for the sake of first confessing to God who received the supplications, he recounts the continuous prayer and the stretching out of the hands through all the nights.

By your power, he says, the whole was set in motion; even the waters groaned in fear, and the abysses had a tumultuous struggle (Ps 76:17-19). And water was being released from above from the clouds, and clouds ran through the ether with much sound, and the arrows from heaven were being carried down; and sounds of thunder were happening according to the airy circle of the clouds passing through, and lightnings were streaming down upon the inhabited world.

And it shook the earth with an earthquake. These things are warning wonders appearing among those in Egypt, those in the wilderness, and those in Judah. For Egypt was struck by hail with fire being carried along, and the Red Sea drew back its waters as if being contracted by some fear. And thunders burst forth in the air and hail was poured down, also against the Canaanites in the war toward the Jews. And it is evident that lightning also flashed together.

Regarding the saying of the thunder sounding in a wheel, one says that it happened when [God] joined the axles of the wagons and led them into the sea with their leaders. Ps 76:19: He lays for us an airy circle upon which the stars are placed, just as oxen circling a threshing floor. For a spherical heaven, according to the logic of the Greeks, is not to be found in the divine oracles, so that we might conceive of the wheel-like revolution above the earth and below the earth. For the divine writings present water below the earth, not heaven, and waters lying beneath as a boundary above the heaven. For He says of the heaven, stretching out like a skin, covering its upper parts with waters. To set the sun from one end to the other, from east to west, and it is said that not even the smallest part of it turns back from the west. And He says of the one who set the heaven (not the one circling it in a circle) and stretching it out like a tent to dwell in (not as circling around); and Isaiah says of the one coming from the ends of the foundation of heaven to those coming from far off the earth, so that the heaven has been founded and stands, but not circling in a circle. But these things are for the sake of a brief reminder, so that we do not fail to be carried toward the fabrications of the Greeks, neglecting the divine writings.

Ps 76:20-21: He says of the divine way that it has no visible trace like the human way; therefore he also called that journey 'in sea and waters,' since Solomon says that a ship traversing the sea is not recognized, so that what is said is parabolic. And there is no longer a journey for God to pass through; for the Hebrews did not walk through the sea so that He might lead them through it as well, but the thing regarding the Red Sea was brief for them, while the thing through the land was much and long-lasting. You guided as sheep your people in the hand of Moses and Aaron. Moreover, even though unseen by...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The fate of the righteous in the destruction of Jerusalem
english: Since the journey was occurring, it became known and manifest to men that I would guide the people in the journey from Egypt as sheep led by Moses and Aaron. Thus indeed the psalm is a parable ...

[Others have interpreted these things thus:] The aforementioned psalm ended in silence, neither seeking nor stating the causes for which the people were so greatly lifted up against their guardian God; but this indicates the cause of the turning away from God from above, which God also later through Isaiah expressed by saying: 'Is not the hand of the Lord too weak to save? Or was the ear too heavy to hear?' (Isa 59:1). But your sins divide you between yourselves and God, and because of your sins He turned His face from you so as not to show mercy, and the following things. Therefore, there is a memory in the psalm of the distrust and contention in the wilderness of Israel, so as to show those turning away from God the evil causes becoming to themselves, as David clearly narrates the things. And it begins royally, immediately commanding his own people to attend to the proper law, or to private instructions, as an Ally interprets; for, he says, such a law is to bring forth a ready exhortation.

And if he says that not the philanthropy and pity of God and much propitiation preserved their succession, but with all passion He struck them, they would have perished, and they became anonymous; [he says] not having accepted their choice, but pitying their weakness as if flesh were rotting and spirit was departing.

[The interpreters have set forth the hypothesis of this psalm differently. For one says that the prophet is stripped simply of captivity and the things that happened to Jerusalem, without specifying which; another says it makes manifest the [captivity] under the Romans which happened after the betrayal of our Savior Jesus Christ; others [say] the one under Antiochus Epiphanus. Therefore, having done this, let us examine some of the sayings.] The intercession against the nations is that, having been impious and unclean, they despoiled a holy land and defiled a holy temple; but against Jerusalem, the contrary, that a city called holy has become a heap of dust and stones.

Which Theodotion says is regarding lithology. And these things can be a remembrance of the election concerning Jerusalem that has occurred. Furthermore, regarding their inhabitants, the [Psalmist] says 'the merciful', that even after death the unburied were given as food to the birds, which proves much and something raw regarding the enemies of the defeated and the slaves of God who suffered these things, which can be brought near to God and for supplication to the Lord.

For even if complaints against the slaves be just, it is unhuman for mercy regarding one's own to be administered by a stranger. And he says also that the bodies of the holy became food for beasts and their blood was poured out without mercy like water before Jerusalem; perhaps indeed because of the election from the beginning, he calls those who fell away holy, just as also the Apostle says of the holy [vine] that those cut off through impiety [are also holy] (because they were of the holy root), perhaps he also indicates the holy ones as being perished together with [the wicked] to the unrighteous, which happens in the capture and the destruction of both a city and a nation, and this has been revealed through Ezekiel; for he says: 'The Lord says, Behold, I am with you, and I will stretch out my hand from its cradle and will destroy from you, the just and the impious, and I will cut off from you the just and the impious' (Ezekiel 7:9).

Which was also foretold more allegorically thus: 'Behold, I kindle fire in you, and every wood shall be consumed in you, the moist and every dry wood' (Ezekiel 20:33); the moist being allegorically the wood of the righteous man, and the dry the impious, just as the Lord himself revealed the true righteous wood saying, 'If these are doing such things in the moist wood, what happens in the dry?'

And if the Lord shared in those things coming upon the world according to the flesh, yet shared in no sin, it is not wonderful that righteous men, being partakers of sin, should become partakers of the misfortunes which come through sins, to suffer equally with the unrighteous being murdered, just as he himself was reckoned among the lawless (Hebrews 2:9), yet was judged by God; such as was the case with Jeremiah, being taken among the impious captives, yet having some distinction also among men after the captivity in the honor from the one who had captured him. And the righteous one would continue to share with the sinners even unto death.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Vine and the Feast of Booths
english: Being so, by this the things after death are already useful for distinguishing the separation from the evil ones, just as for King Josiah; for he indeed, being righteous, also died in war while Egypt was prevailing, and much Israelite impiety had already come to pass and did not receive forgiveness. Therefore for those righteous, if they suffer along with the sinners, there are set aside from God things more beautiful after the suffering; and indeed for the brothers and kinsmen who suffer through sin, much assistance is set aside through them, so that because of their turning away, a certain turning of God toward the race might come to pass, which even now the prophet deserves. These things were lifted up as acceptable righteousness before God (Ps 78:4). For if even we are worthy, he says, of those whom we have suffered, but your name is shared in conscience, just as God himself through Isaiah says, 'Through all things my name is blasphemed among the nations' (Isa 56:5). Because like the judgment of beasts, he says, the God-fearing nation was desolated and they laid waste the holy land (Ps 78:7).

Sitting upon the cherubim, having named the authority, he makes manifest the heavenly authority through which everything is subject to him and nothing is able to withstand, if only it should appear; and he calls for the power to be raised because of the remaining silent and quiet and seeing the people suffering; just as it was suffered to come to an end by the Assyrians, not presently, they deserve it because of the abandonment. How, then, to come, either according to the energy or [otherwise]? Because of this he says, 'Come to save us,' just as if he were saying, 'Come according to the saving.' But the 'Turn to us and shine your face,' because of the appearance, the one turned away from God is not able to encounter, unless he first turns back toward him; 'Turn to me,' he says, 'and I will turn to you.' He asks for this from the guidance and cooperation of God, such as is also, 'Incline my heart to your testimonies' (Ps 119:36). For the pious entrust the whole universe to God. But if you appear, he says, 'your face,' and we shall be saved; for the appearance of God is salvation (Ps 79:9). With the eighteenth shadow, indeed, the aforementioned vine covered the mountains because of all the height and surpassed all power that is above the earth, and with the outstretching of the unblemished ones, the cedars of God [were moved] because of the divine power...

To be surrounded, it extends both to the sea and the river. For even the boundaries of the land of Judah are thus called by God: from the wilderness to the Euphrates and from the Red Sea to the Philistine sea. Which [vine] therefore He, He says, brought out of Egypt and transplanted a vine, which He thus made manifest and so widely spread out; why then was it surrounded thus, having been stripped of its protection and being harvested by those passing by?

Trumpets begin at the new moons according to the law. At the new moon of the seventh month He commanded the sounding of trumpets, and on the fifteenth [day] the feast of the booths. And this was a gathering of fruits at the end of the year in the assembly of the works from the field, as has been declared in Exodus (Exod 23:16). And it might be to the one spiritually contemplating the law that the trumpet is a sign of the trumpets coming from heaven, and the fast appointed for atonement in the tenth of that same month is the month of that which is said by the Lord: 'Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted' (Matt 5:4). For the law, preparing for the rest of the booths and the joy in it, made the fast and the humility in it, introducing the trumpets which declare the fear of the presence of the Judge from heaven. Of these, the humility for atonement follows, announcing the coming judgment, and thus the feast for rest comes to be.

And the psalm, being sung at the new moons, let it be even at the time of the feast, differing according to the custom of the law, and for this reason mentioning trumpets at the beginning as a prelude to the feast of booths. Let it signify this: the end about which even the inscription sings to it, declares; when God has gathered all the fruits, and gives eternal booths to His own. For in that end, the good things are restored to the ones being saved, and the salvation from the evils of the present, for which the aforementioned psalms were making supplications to God. [The following things follow after it.]

Removals, that is, of the burdens, of the swellings; for those serving the brick-making, cutting the clay with a spade, they carry it on their backs. Their back, therefore, He says, stood away from swellings, that is, He freed it from the burdens (Ps 80:7).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
